samples.question: Two rows of nine square cells stand on a white card, one above the other; each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Beneath a cell of each row a small dark arrowhead points straight up at that one cell, marking it.  Imagine that marked cell is removed from each row entirely and the remaining cells are slid together to close the gap, keeping their left-to-right order.  Those shortened eight-cell rows are not drawn anywhere; only after withdrawing each marked cell do they exist.  Do the two surviving rows then read the same in dark and pale, cell for cell?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.
